no_claim: This proves the bounded F1-F10 foundation: owner-local MC2 Level 1 plus four semantic extension surfaces. It does not prove whole MC2, arbitrary games, production generated assets, VR, voxels, cities, water, multiplayer, or commercial release.

requirements.positive: MC2-owned and custom.synthetic validate to the same versioned definition model with canonical graph identities.
requirements.negative: Malformed members, graph cycles, collisions, hash drift, and path escape are rejected before publication.
requirements.proof_layer: Rust definition loader plus final artifact inventory.

requirements.positive: The engine capability registry satisfies exact package requirements.
requirements.negative: Unknown or wrong capability versions and package-provided executable capability are rejected.
requirements.proof_layer: Rust package validation.

requirements.positive: All four writable descriptors have structural read, validate, apply, and read-back bindings.
requirements.negative: Duplicate, missing, catalog-only, and undiscoverable bindings are rejected.
requirements.proof_layer: Rust catalog structure and public CLI read-back.

requirements.positive: The independent Level 1 source census covers the four bounded semantic surfaces.
requirements.negative: A planted consumed constant or source fingerprint drift is rejected.
requirements.proof_layer: Independent source-census conformance test.

requirements.positive: Validate and diff preserve the authoritative workspace root.
requirements.negative: Malformed and partial candidates prove the root digest is unchanged after refusal.
requirements.proof_layer: Rust transaction fault tests plus black-box workspace digests.

requirements.positive: Apply publishes one immutable CAS-guarded definition and returns read-back evidence.
requirements.negative: A stale definition guard fails without changing the root.
requirements.proof_layer: Rust transaction tests plus black-box stale-CAS refusal.

requirements.positive: Existing sessions remain definition-bound until reset or reopen advances generation.
requirements.negative: Publication alone cannot alter either simultaneous live session.
requirements.proof_layer: Rust domain-session isolation and native session guard tests.

requirements.positive: Definition, graphs, assets, and receipt become visible at one recoverable commit point.
requirements.negative: Injected pre/post-boundary interruption cannot expose a partial state.
requirements.proof_layer: Rust durable fault injection and killed-CLI recovery tests.

requirements.positive: Rollback is a new guarded publication to a retained content-addressed graph.
requirements.negative: Stale guards, absent retained graphs, and tampered retained artifacts refuse without mutation.
requirements.proof_layer: Rust forward-rollback tests.

requirements.positive: The built native plugin opens and runs the neutral Level 1 route using real owner inputs.
requirements.negative: Mock, empty, internal-only, and missing-owner routes cannot satisfy the selected black-box cases.
requirements.proof_layer: External ctypes consumer of the versioned C ABI.

requirements.positive: The current non-no-op Level 1 route matches fixed accepted state, event, audio, and presentation observations.
requirements.negative: Any fixed value, order, identity, runtime-pin, or selected-case discrepancy fails.
requirements.proof_layer: Pinned reference corpus and current-source native black box.

requirements.positive: Neutral and sealed compatibility routes agree in the same current-source build.
requirements.negative: Differential agreement cannot override a fixed-corpus mismatch.
requirements.proof_layer: Same-build differential plus fixed reference corpus.

requirements.positive: The flight-only package changes the ordinary target-speed clamp, integration, and displacement.
requirements.negative: Removing the flight binding restores custom baseline while mana, objectives, action sequence, and event IDs remain countermetrics.
requirements.proof_layer: Same-trace native, Unity, and TypeScript observations.

requirements.positive: The spell-only package changes the mana debit of an ordinary Fireball cast.
requirements.negative: Removing the spell binding restores custom baseline; pose, motion, objectives, action sequence, and event IDs remain countermetrics.
requirements.proof_layer: Same-trace native, Unity, and TypeScript observations.

requirements.positive: The enemy-policy-only package changes the ordinary Goat lifecycle and emits identified engagement boundaries.
requirements.negative: Removing the policy restores zero baseline engagements; non-engagement event order and player countermetrics remain unchanged.
requirements.proof_layer: Same-trace native, Unity, and TypeScript lifecycle observations.

requirements.positive: The asset-only package changes a typed indexed-sprite payload at real Unity and TypeScript cache invalidation boundaries.
requirements.negative: Removing the asset binding restores baseline payload identity; stable reads reuse the cache and gameplay is unchanged.
requirements.proof_layer: Native payload read plus actual Unity Texture2D and TypeScript RGBA caches.

requirements.positive: Baseline, four one-factor runs, and combined custom run share exact engine and client executables; combined observations equal the four declared effects.
requirements.negative: Executable drift, undeclared package artifacts, retained effects after factor removal, or a client/package special case fails.
requirements.proof_layer: Hash inventory, package whitelist, and composed same-trace matrix.

requirements.positive: Native, Unity, and TypeScript round-trip one normalized combined command/snapshot/event/asset projection.
requirements.negative: Unknown gameplay fields and lossy u64 transport values are rejected.
requirements.proof_layer: Native JSON domain projection through C#, Python, and Node adapters.

requirements.positive: Zero, one, and seven presentation reads between identical steps preserve snapshots and ordered gameplay events.
requirements.negative: Any polling-dependent state, RNG, or event result fails exact comparison.
requirements.proof_layer: Native polling-invariance sessions plus neutral conformance suite.

requirements.positive: The authored asset binds the complete indexed-sprite type signature and engine budgets.
requirements.negative: Wrong shape, timing, coordinates, palette, dependency, size, path, or hash fails before publication.
requirements.proof_layer: Rust typed asset validator plus native observation.

requirements.positive: Source, recipe, runtime artifacts, and binding are content-addressed and the deterministic recipe rebuilds exactly.
requirements.negative: Tampered source/runtime bytes and failed publication preserve the prior binding.
requirements.proof_layer: Checked transform, manifest inventory, and atomic asset rollback test.

requirements.positive: The frozen Level 1/2 native, Rust, managed, and TypeScript compatibility inventory is complete and owned.
requirements.negative: A missing baseline symbol or disposition is rejected.
requirements.proof_layer: Four-layer compatibility surface guard.

requirements.positive: No new package-specific public symbol or Level-N authority branch appears outside compatibility surfaces.
requirements.negative: Planted native, Rust, managed, and TypeScript package symbols fail structurally.
requirements.proof_layer: Four-layer symbol guard and semantic-ID leak tests.

requirements.positive: Unity and TypeScript only validate, copy, and present Rust observations.
requirements.negative: A client gameplay writer, hidden simulation field, or package-specific client branch fails the surface/parity proof.
requirements.proof_layer: Static compatibility inventory plus runtime cross-client parity.

requirements.positive: Domain errors are typed and state-preserving across package, semantic, session, cursor, and definition conflicts.
requirements.negative: Malformed, unknown, bounds, generation, stale-CAS, tamper, and partial-asset cases are rejected with unchanged roots.
requirements.proof_layer: Rust, CLI, and native negative controls.

requirements.positive: Transport interruption is recoverable through an idempotency key and apply-status receipt.
requirements.negative: Killed-before-commit preserves state; killed-after-commit resolves the exact committed receipt instead of inventing a simulation timeout.
requirements.proof_layer: Real killed-process CLI integration tests.
